hints: Focus on what the mass change is telling you, an increase of 34 must mean atoms have added across the C=C without breaking the carbon chain.
Check what adds up to 34, two O atoms (32) plus two H atoms (2) fits perfectly and points to adding two -OH groups to make a diol.
Recall the two very different roles of acidified manganate(VII), mild addition versus vigorous cleavage, and pick the mild set that keeps the skeleton intact.
walkthrough:
**Decode the mass clue**

Think simply first. If $M_r$ goes up by 34, we have added atoms and we have not cut the molecule in pieces.

Added mass = $34$

**Match 34 to a functional group change**

Adding two hydroxyl groups across the double bond adds $2 \times 16 + 2 \times 1 = 34$.

$$\text{RCH=CHR'} + [O] + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCH(OH)-CH(OH)R'}$$

**Recall the two manganate(VII) conditions**

Cold, dilute $\text{MnO}_4^-$ gives mild syn-addition to a diol. Hot, concentrated $\text{MnO}_4^-$ gives vigorous oxidative cleavage to carbonyls and carboxylic acids, which breaks C-C bonds.

$$\text{alkene} \xrightarrow{\text{cold, dilute } \text{MnO}_4^-} \text{diol}$$

**Choose the conditions**

Since we want the addition product with $M_r$ increased by 34, we need the mild conditions that form the diol and avoid cleavage.

options.A: Cold is correct for mild oxidation, but concentrated manganate(VII) is too vigorous. The diol test requires cold, dilute conditions to stop at addition without further oxidation.
options.B: Cold, dilute acidified MnO4- gives mild hydroxylation of the C=C to a diol. Two -OH groups add across the bond, increasing Mr by 34, exactly as required.
options.C: Hot, concentrated MnO4- causes full oxidative cleavage of the C=C to give aldehydes, ketones and then carboxylic acids. The carbon chain is broken, so Mr would fall, not rise by 34.
options.D: Heating makes the oxidation vigorous even if dilute, so cleavage still occurs. Hot conditions do not stop at the diol, so you would not get the +34 addition product.
